human_authorisation.authorisation_note: User asked to scope out and then activate the last remaining candidate registry, exercise_activity_applicability_registry. The source candidate (S-REG-09) covered only 4 of 19 exercises, only the training context, and one exercise (front_plank) does not exist in the live exercise registry. Full activation required a genuinely complete closure, not a data conversion. The repository owner confirmed two derivation rules by explicit decision: (1) an exercise applies to an activity iff its pattern is in that activity's allowed_movement_ids, with back_squat/deadlift/bench_press getting primary=powerlifting and every other exercise getting primary=general_strength (implemented in S-REG-32); (2) all 3 required contexts (training/testing/competition) use identical applicability values. This slice builds the full 159-record closure on top of S-REG-32's schema extension and evolves the S-V1-23 guard from a must-not-exist block into real coverage enforcement, mirroring S-V1-22's (equipment) prior evolution during S-REG-25.

rollback_plan.primary: git revert <this-slice-commit> - reverses every data file (registries/exercise_activity_applicability/exercise_activity_applicability.registry.json, ci/schemas/exercise_activity_applicability.registry.schema.json, registry_index.json, registry_bundle.json, registry_surface_classification.json, the four seal evidence files, the S-V1-23 guard/doc evolution, and this slice's own scaffolding) atomically back to the pre-activation sealed state in one step.
